requirement:
The book's coverage overview identifies files by their workspace-relative
paths and connects each file to its documented `habeas:coverage` annotations.
It reports documentation, rather than measured execution percentages or a
coverage-policy verdict.
rationale: Obligations from `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`: (1) files are identified by workspace-relative paths; (2) each file is connected to its documented `habeas:coverage` annotations; (3) the overview reports documentation only, with no measured execution percentages and no coverage-policy verdict. 1. Workspace-relative paths. `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documented_items_are_counted_once_with_browsable_directory_and_file_groups]` uses a temporary workspace with files at the root and in nested directories (`code.rs`, `src/direct.rs`, `src/deep/nested.rs`, `vendor/foreign.rs`, `docs_only/deep/item.rs`). It asserts `data-file="code.rs"`, the directory groups `src`, `src/deep` and `docs_only/deep`, the contents lists via `assert_directory_contents`, and `{file}:{line} #{selector}` locations. The temporary root path never appears in these assertions. It also asserts that `src/pass.rs`, which has no annotation, is not listed. 2. Connecting each file to its annotations. For each of the three file cards, the same test asserts the following: - The card has a link to the per-file notes page, and the expected href is computed from `notes::path` and `chapter_href`. - The card shows the annotation count (1 or 2). - The card links to `#coverage-note-{ordinal}` for every ordinal. - The notes chapter exists at that path and has a matching `File: file` heading and matching `id="coverage-note-N"` anchors. - The card shows the annotation's explanation text (root, function, or the "No tracked justification" default). - The card shows the per-item locations. The test also asserts that exactly 5 notes chapters exist and that the total is "7 documented source items", so annotations are counted once. 3. Documentation only, with no measurement or verdict. The first test asserts that `CI would`, `instrumented lines covered`, `gap-percentage`, `gap-verdict` and `data-status=` are absent. `book_ignores_saved_measurements_and_preserves_artifacts` records a saved measurement attempt, with valid, invalid and `{}` metadata. It asserts that the rendered book is identical to the one rendered without measurements and that the saved test name never appears. It also asserts that `Line coverage:`, `selected test attempts`, `0 unresolved gaps` and similar measurement text are absent. Finally it asserts that the overview says `habeas coverage-check` enforces measured coverage, so the overview itself does not report it. Both tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no obligation without a test or assertion, and no marking gap.
